subtopics.title: Forwarding vs. Routing in the Network Layer
subtopics.summary: Introduces the two key network-layer functions: forwarding, the per-router data-plane function that moves a datagram from an input link to an output link, and routing, the control-plane, network-wide function that determines the end-to-end path a datagram takes from source to destination host.

subtopics.title: Router Input and Output Ports
subtopics.summary: Covers the internal operations of a router's input and output ports: how arriving packets are processed and looked up on input links, and how packets are prepared and transmitted onto output links.

subtopics.title: Switching Fabric and Packet Queues
subtopics.summary: Examines a router's internal switching mechanisms that move packets from input ports to output ports, and packet queue management, including where queues form inside a router and how they are managed.

subtopics.title: Traditional IP Forwarding
subtopics.summary: Covers destination-based forwarding, where a router forwards a datagram based on the destination address in the datagram's header by matching it against entries in the forwarding table.

subtopics.title: Generalized Forwarding
subtopics.summary: Covers generalized forwarding, in which forwarding and other packet-processing functions are performed using values from several different fields in the datagram's header rather than the destination address alone.

subtopics.title: Software-Defined Networking (SDN)
subtopics.summary: Describes how SDN explicitly separates the data plane from the control plane: the routing device performs forwarding only, while a remote, software-implemented controller computes and distributes forwarding tables to the routers.
